nodes.title: Least Singular Value of Random Matrices (Rudelson-Vershynin picture)
nodes.body: For an n by n random matrix A with iid mean-zero sub-Gaussian entries, the smallest singular value satisfies P(s_min(A) <= eps n^{-1/2}) <= C eps + c^n: square random matrices are typically invertible with s_min of order n^{-1/2} (Rudelson-Vershynin), resolving the quantitative invertibility problem behind Spielman-Teng smoothed analysis. For tall m by n matrices with m >= (1 + delta) n, s_min is of order sqrt(m) - sqrt(n-ish) with exponential concentration. The proofs decompose the sphere into compressible vectors (close to sparse - handled by nets and tensorization) and incompressible vectors (reduced to distance-to-subspace and small-ball estimates via the Berry-Esseen or Littlewood-Offord theory of anti-concentration).

nodes.title: Smallest Singular Value of a Square Random Matrix (Rudelson-Vershynin)
nodes.body:
Let A be an n x n random matrix whose entries are independent, identically distributed, centred, of unit variance and sub-Gaussian (sub-Gaussian norm at most K). Then for every epsilon >= 0, P( s_min(A) <= epsilon n^{-1/2} ) <= C epsilon + c^n, where C > 0 and c in (0,1) depend only on K. So the smallest singular value of a square random matrix is of order n^{-1/2} with high probability - the same order as for the Gaussian case, where Edelman computed the exact law of n s_min(G)^2 - and A is invertible with probability 1 - c^n even for Bernoulli (+-1) entries, for which singularity has positive probability; the c^n term is necessary because two equal rows occur with probability at least 2^{-n} c'. Together with Gordon's bound for tall matrices this settles the invertibility question for the basic random-matrix models.
entries i.i.d., mean zero, variance one, sub-Gaussian with norm at most K
A is square, n x n
C and c depend only on K; the c^n term cannot be removed for discrete entries

nodes.title: Open problem: Spielman-Teng conjecture on the least singular value of Bernoulli matrices
nodes.body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). For X with i.i.d. symmetric Bernoulli entries, show P(sqrt n s_n(X) <= t) <= t + c^n for some 0 < c < 1, all large n and all small t >= 0. Source: Bordenave and Chafai: Around the circular law, survey with open problems, Section 7, p. 53. Status notes: Bounded recall 2026-09-07: the t = 0 case, P(s_n = 0) = (1/2 + o(1))^n, was proved by Tikhomirov (Ann. Math. 2020); Rudelson-Vershynin (2008) give C t + c^n with an absolute constant C. Whether C can be taken equal to 1 as conjectured was not found resolved.
Posed in Bordenave and Chafai: Around the circular law, survey with open problems
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07

nodes.title: Attempt on Spielman-Teng conjecture on the least singular value of Bernoulli matrices
nodes.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Test whether the constant 1 in front of t is forced by the Gaussian comparison and whether the Bernoulli case can beat it. Result: For the Gaussian matrix Edelman's exact law gives P(sqrt n s_n <= t) = 1 - e^{-t^2/2 - t} ~ t as t -> 0, so the constant 1 is exactly the Gaussian density at zero of sqrt n s_n; the conjecture says Bernoulli matrices are no worse than Gaussian up to the exponentially small singular mass. A sufficient condition would be a local limit theorem for sqrt n s_n at zero uniform in n, which is a universality statement at the hard edge (the smallest singular value) and is known (Tao-Vu 2010 hard-edge universality) only in the form P(sqrt n s_n <= t) = (1 - e^{-t^2/2-t}) + O(n^{-c}) for t in a fixed range, which gives the conjecture for t >= n^{-c'} but not for t between c^n and n^{-c'}. The gap regime is exactly the small-ball regime where the Rudelson-Vershynin constant C appears. No improvement obtained. Key identity: Gaussian case: P(sqrt n s_n <= t) = 1 - exp(-t^2/2 - t), so the conjectured constant is the Gaussian value. Obstruction: Hard-edge universality covers t >= n^{-c}; the conjecture needs the constant 1 down to exponentially small t.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0029-spielman-teng-conjecture-on-the-least-singular-value-of-bernoulli-matr
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

nodes.title: Attempt on Least singular values at the polynomial constant term
nodes.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Least singular values at the polynomial constant term structural calculation Result: For a monomial P=X_(i1)...X_(id), the missing shift is0 and the estimate reduces to the individual matrices. Since smin(P)>=product_k smin(X_(ik)), the event smin(P)<=epsilon implies at least one factor has smin<=epsilon^(1/d). The standard complex-Ginibre bound then gives P(smin(P)<=epsilon)<=C*d*N^2*epsilon^(2/d). Repeated factors require no independence in this union bound. Check: For normalized complex Ginibre, N*smin has the usual bounded quadratic lower tail. Multiply the deterministic singular-value inequalities successively, and apply the union bound over the d factor positions. Obstruction: Sums of monomials can cancel, so this argument gives no least-singular-value estimate for an arbitrary noncommutative polynomial at its constant term.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0191-least-singular-values-at-the-polynomial-constant-term
No independent review

nodes.title: \aleph_\omega is the Smallest Singular Cardinal
nodes.body:
The cardinal \aleph_\omega is a singular cardinal with cofinality \mathrm{cf}(\aleph_\omega) = \omega < \aleph_\omega.
Definition of aleph sequence

nodes.title: Extreme least singular value of random row submatrices under a bounded fourth moment
nodes.body:
Let $\xi_m$ be centered real entry laws (a single fixed law is allowed) satisfying, uniformly in $m$, $\operatorname{Var}(\xi_m)=1$, $\|f_{\xi_m}\|_\infty \le K$ for a density $f_{\xi_m}$, and $\mathbb{E}|\xi_m|^4 \le B < \infty$. Let $A_m \in \mathbb{R}^{N_m \times m}$ have iid entries with law $\xi_m$ and $N_m/m \to \gamma > 1$. For a surplus $r_m \ge 0$ put $M_{m,r_m}(A_m) = \min_{T \subset [N_m],\,|T| = m + r_m} \sigma_m((A_m)_T)$ and $k_m = r_m + 1$. If $k_m \log m = o(m)$, then $\frac{k_m}{m}\log M_{m,r_m}(A_m) \to -h(\gamma)$ in probability, where $h(\gamma) = \gamma\log\gamma - (\gamma-1)\log(\gamma-1)$. For fixed $r$ this reads $\frac{1}{m}\log M_{m,r} \to -h(\gamma)/(r+1)$. STATUS, recorded as the source states it and deliberately not upgraded: this is a CANDIDATE COMPLETE PROOF and still requires two independent audits before closure. It weakens the subgaussian hypothesis of the published version (arXiv:2608.07410, Yang-Wen-Shmalo) to a uniform fourth moment, but does NOT retain that paper's explicit $Ce^{-c\sqrt{m}}$ deviation rate or its compact-aspect-ratio uniform almost-sure formulation. The complex analogue, and its factor $1/2$, remain OPEN.
entries iid, centered, variance one
uniformly bounded density
uniformly bounded fourth moment
N_m/m -> gamma > 1
k_m log m = o(m)

nodes.title: The Frobenius separation of the Sylvester operator is the smallest singular value of I kron A - B^T kron I
nodes.body:
For complex matrices A (n by n) and B (m by m), S(X) = AX - XB on n by m matrices X, and the Frobenius separation is sep_F(A, B) = min over ||X||_F = 1 of ||AX - XB||_F. With column stacking, vec(AX - XB) = (I_m kron A - B^T kron I_n) vec(X), so sep_F(A, B) is the smallest singular value of I_m kron A - B^T kron I_n.
A is n by n and B is m by m, complex

nodes.title: Smallest singular value
nodes.body: $s_n(A)=\min_{\|x\|_2=1}\|Ax\|_2$; for an $n\times n$ matrix with i.i.d. subgaussian entries $P(s_n(A)\le\varepsilon n^{-1/2})\le C\varepsilon+e^{-cn}$ (Rudelson-Vershynin).
